extraction.Name: Joseph Mousseau
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent to his 480 allotment when it was issued, September 29, 1919, but it was sent to him through the mail, and he was given to understand that, if he did not accept the patent, the land would be taxed, and later sold for same; so he took the patent in fee
extraction.Buyer: sold to Mr. Cherry, of Martin, South Dakota, for $2400.00, $1600.00 in cash, and received notes to secure the balance of the purchase price
extraction.Occupation/Income: he and his wife each still have a quarter of land that they rent, which brings them in a small yearly income; and that this is their only source of income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; very poor health, being badly crippled, and unable to work; has his wife and a grandson to support; wife is old and feeble; grandson has good health; did not sell land for indebtedness incurred prior to receiving the patent in fee; Mr. Cherry never paid the notes off and told deponent he could sell them to other people; other people offered $25.00 to $50.00 each for the notes; deponent considers he got a real poor price for his land as well as poor treatment from the purchaser; has never received any aid from the county, State nor the United States Government; allotment was 480 acres; sworn February 25, 1929 | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County, South Dakota" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')

recovery_notes.rationale: Pine Ridge tribe field had 40+ string variants across the corpus. Consolidating to canonical 'Pine Ridge' for clean tabulation while preserving original variant in NOTES for audit.
